claim: M-CSF-dependent monocyte-derived macrophages (M-MØ) exhibit higher levels of Ser21-GSK3α phosphorylation compared to GM-CSF-dependent macrophages (GM-MØ).
source: Ser21-GSK3α and Ser9-GSK3β phosphorylation was more pronounced in M-MØ, aligning with their elevated levels of MAFB (Figure 1A).
evidence: Western blot data showing phosphorylation levels in M-MØ vs GM-MØ with statistical analysis (p<0.005)

claim: M-CSF-dependent monocyte-derived macrophages (M-MØ) exhibit higher levels of Ser9-GSK3β phosphorylation compared to GM-CSF-dependent macrophages (GM-MØ).
source: Ser21-GSK3α and Ser9-GSK3β phosphorylation was more pronounced in M-MØ, aligning with their elevated levels of MAFB (Figure 1A).
evidence: Western blot data showing phosphorylation levels in M-MØ vs GM-MØ with statistical analysis (p<0.005)

claim: M-MØ have elevated levels of MAFB protein compared to GM-MØ.
source: Ser21-GSK3α and Ser9-GSK3β phosphorylation was more pronounced in M-MØ, aligning with their elevated levels of MAFB (Figure 1A).
evidence: Western blot data showing MAFB protein levels with statistical analysis (p<0.001)

claim: There is no significant difference in Tyr279-GSK3α phosphorylation between M-MØ and GM-MØ.
source: Conversely, no significant difference in Tyr279-GSK3α and Tyr216-GSK3β phosphorylation was observed between M-MØ and GM-MØ (Figure 1B).
evidence: Western blot data with statistical analysis showing no significant difference

claim: There is no significant difference in Tyr216-GSK3β phosphorylation between M-MØ and GM-MØ.
source: Conversely, no significant difference in Tyr279-GSK3α and Tyr216-GSK3β phosphorylation was observed between M-MØ and GM-MØ (Figure 1B).
evidence: Western blot data with statistical analysis showing no significant difference

claim: The heightened expression of MAFB in M-MØ correlates with higher inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3.
source: Therefore, the heightened expression of MAFB in M-MØ correlates with a higher inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3.
evidence: Correlation observed between MAFB levels and GSK3 phosphorylation patterns in experimental data

claim: Treatment of GM-MØ with CHIR-99021 for 48 hr results in a significant decrease in activation-associated Tyr216-GSK3β phosphorylation.
source: Indeed, treatment of GM-MØ with CHIR-99021 for 48 hr resulted in a significant decrease in the activation-associated Tyr216-GSK3β phosphorylation (Figure 1D) and a robust elevation in MAFB protein levels (Figure 1E).
evidence: Western blot data showing decreased Tyr216-GSK3β phosphorylation after CHIR-99021 treatment with statistical significance (p<0.001)

claim: Treatment of GM-MØ with CHIR-99021 for 48 hr results in a robust elevation in MAFB protein levels.
source: Indeed, treatment of GM-MØ with CHIR-99021 for 48 hr resulted in a significant decrease in the activation-associated Tyr216-GSK3β phosphorylation (Figure 1D) and a robust elevation in MAFB protein levels (Figure 1E).
evidence: Western blot data showing increased MAFB protein levels after CHIR-99021 treatment

claim: GSK3 inhibition in GM-MØ results in more than 2000 differentially expressed genes.
source: RNA-Seq analysis of CHIR-GM-MØ unveiled a huge transcriptional impact of GSK3 inhibition, with more than 2000 differentially expressed genes ([log2FC]>1; adjp<0.05) (Figure 1F).
evidence: RNA-Seq data analysis showing differential gene expression with specified statistical thresholds

claim: The CHIR-GM-MØ transcriptome is significantly enriched in genes that mark M-MØ.
source: Corresponding with the higher MAFB expression, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that the CHIR-GM-MØ transcriptome was significantly enriched in genes that either mark M-MØ (GSE68061) or are upregulated during monocyte-to-M-MØ differentiation (Figure 1G).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of M-MØ marker genes in CHIR-GM-MØ

claim: GM-MØ-specific genes are downregulated in CHIR-GM-MØ.
source: Conversely, GM-MØ-specific genes (GSE68061) or genes increased during monocyte-to-GM-MØ differentiation were downregulated (Figure 1G).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing downregulation of GM-MØ-specific genes

claim: GSK3 inhibition augments the expression of gene sets that define long-term resident macrophages (Cluster HES1_Mac #2).
source: Thus, analysis of the MoMac-VERSE (a resource that identified conserved monocyte and macrophage states derived from healthy and pathologic human tissues) (GSE178209) Mulder et al., 2021 indicated that GSK3 inhibition augments the expression of the gene sets that define MoMac-VERSE subsets identified as long-term resident macrophages [Cluster HES1_Mac (#2)] and tumor-associated macrophages with an M2-like signature [Clusters HES1_Mac (#2), TREM2_Mac (#3), C1Qhi_Mac (#16) and FTL_Mac (#17)] (Mulder et al., 2021; Figure 1H).
evidence: GSEA analysis of MoMac-VERSE gene sets showing enrichment in CHIR-GM-MØ

claim: GSK3 inhibition increases the expression of gene sets that define pathogenic pro-fibrotic macrophage subsets in severe COVID-19.
source: Moreover, GSK3 inhibition increased the expression of the gene sets that define pathogenic pro-fibrotic macrophage subsets in severe COVID-19 ([Group 3 or SPP1+, GSE145926] [Liao et al., 2020], MoAM3 [GSE155249] [Grant et al., 2021] or CD163+/LGMN+ MØ [EGAS00001005634] [Wendisch et al., 2021]) (Figure 1I).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of COVID-19 pathogenic macrophage gene sets

claim: GSK3 inhibition enhances MAFB expression and reprograms macrophages by promoting the acquisition of the gene profile that defines anti-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic macrophages.
source: Therefore, GSK3 inhibition enhances MAFB expression and reprograms macrophages by promoting the acquisition of the gene profile that defines anti-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic macrophages.
evidence: Summary of multiple experimental findings including MAFB expression and gene profile changes

claim: DoRoThEA analysis reveals a significant enrichment in MAFB-regulated genes in CHIR-GM-MØ.
source: In agreement with the increased MAFB levels detected in CHIR-GM-MØ (Figure 1E), screening for mediators of the reprogramming action of GSK3 inhibition using DoRoThEA (Garcia-Alonso et al., 2019; https://saezlab.github.io/dorothea/; Badia-i-Mompel et al., 2019) revealed a significant enrichment in MAFB-regulated genes (Figure 2A), and similar results were yielded upon Enrichr analysis (Kuleshov et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2013) (https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: DoRoThEA computational analysis showing MAFB enrichment

claim: CHIR-GM-MØ are enriched in MAFB-dependent genes.
source: In fact, GSEA confirmed that CHIR-GM-MØ are enriched in MAFB-dependent genes (Vega et al., 2020; Cuevas et al., 2017; Figure 2B and C) along with macrophage genes whose regulatory regions are directly bound by MAFB (Simón-Fuentes et al., 2023) (75-geneset, Figure 2C), including CCL2, CCL8, CCL18, IGF1, IL10, and LGMN (Figure 2D).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of MAFB-dependent genes with specific gene examples

claim: CHIR-GM-MØ show elevated expression of the transcription factor MAF.
source: Importantly, all these changes were reflected in the phenotype of CHIR-GM-MØ, which showed elevated expression of transcription factors like MAF (Figure 2E), cell surface proteins like CD163 and FOLR2 (Figure 2E and F), and soluble factors like CCL2, CCL18, IL-10, LGMN, and SPP1 (Figure 2G), all of which are either direct MAFB targets (Simón-Fuentes et al., 2023) or MAFB-regulated genes (Vega et al., 2020; Cuevas et al., 2017).
evidence: Western blot data showing increased MAF protein levels

claim: CHIR-GM-MØ show elevated expression of cell surface proteins CD163 and FOLR2.
source: Importantly, all these changes were reflected in the phenotype of CHIR-GM-MØ, which showed elevated expression of transcription factors like MAF (Figure 2E), cell surface proteins like CD163 and FOLR2 (Figure 2E and F), and soluble factors like CCL2, CCL18, IL-10, LGMN, and SPP1 (Figure 2G), all of which are either direct MAFB targets (Simón-Fuentes et al., 2023) or MAFB-regulated genes (Vega et al., 2020; Cuevas et al., 2017).
evidence: Western blot data showing increased CD163 and FOLR2 protein levels with statistical significance

claim: CHIR-GM-MØ show elevated production of soluble factors CCL2, CCL18, IL-10, LGMN, and SPP1.
source: Importantly, all these changes were reflected in the phenotype of CHIR-GM-MØ, which showed elevated expression of transcription factors like MAF (Figure 2E), cell surface proteins like CD163 and FOLR2 (Figure 2E and F), and soluble factors like CCL2, CCL18, IL-10, LGMN, and SPP1 (Figure 2G), all of which are either direct MAFB targets (Simón-Fuentes et al., 2023) or MAFB-regulated genes (Vega et al., 2020; Cuevas et al., 2017).
evidence: ELISA data showing increased production of these soluble factors with statistical significance

claim: CHIR-GM-MØ show decreased production of Activin A.
source: Likewise, the attenuated expression of the GM-MØ-specific INHBA gene (Figure 2D) corresponded to a decrease in Activin A production by CHIR-GM-MØ (Figure 2G).
evidence: RNA-Seq data showing decreased INHBA expression and ELISA data showing decreased Activin A production

claim: CHIR-GM-MØ exhibited elevated anti-inflammatory activity, evidenced by increased production of IL-10 upon activation by inflammatory cytokines or PAMPs.
source: Thus, CHIR-GM-MØ exhibited elevated anti-inflammatory activity, evidenced by increased production of IL-10 upon activation by inflammatory cytokines such as TNF or IFNγ, or exposure to PAMPs like LPS or the TLR7 ligand CL264 (Figure 3A).
evidence: ELISA data showing increased IL-10 production under various stimulation conditions with statistical significance

claim: CHIR-GM-MØ demonstrated increased phagocytic ability for Escherichia coli particles.
source: In addition, CHIR-GM-MØ demonstrated increased phagocytic ability for Escherichia coli particles (Figure 3B), as well as enhanced efferocytosis (Figure 3C), with both activities being typically higher in M-MØ.
evidence: Flow cytometry data showing increased phagocytosis with statistical significance (p<0.05)

claim: CHIR-GM-MØ demonstrated enhanced efferocytosis.
source: In addition, CHIR-GM-MØ demonstrated increased phagocytic ability for Escherichia coli particles (Figure 3B), as well as enhanced efferocytosis (Figure 3C), with both activities being typically higher in M-MØ.
evidence: Flow cytometry data showing enhanced efferocytosis with statistical significance

claim: GSK3 inhibition induced modifications in various metabolic parameters in GM-MØ, including basal respiration and maximal ATP production.
source: Of note, in line with the well-established connection between inflammatory potential and metabolic state in macrophages (Wculek et al., 2022), GSK3 inhibition also induced modifications in various metabolic parameters in GM-MØ, including basal respiration and maximal ATP production (Figure 3—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: Seahorse bioenergetics data showing changes in metabolic parameters with statistical significance

claim: Silencing of both GSK3A and GSK3B augmented the expression of MAFB.
source: Like CHIR-99021, silencing of both GSK3A and GSK3B augmented the expression of MAFB, with the simultaneous silencing of both GSK3A and GSK3B genes having a stronger effect (Figure 4B) and modulated the expression of 329 genes (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: Western blot data showing increased MAFB after siRNA knockdown

claim: Simultaneous silencing of both GSK3A and GSK3B has a stronger effect on MAFB expression than silencing either gene alone.
source: Like CHIR-99021, silencing of both GSK3A and GSK3B augmented the expression of MAFB, with the simultaneous silencing of both GSK3A and GSK3B genes having a stronger effect (Figure 4B) and modulated the expression of 329 genes (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: Western blot data comparing MAFB levels after single vs. double knockdown

claim: GSK3A/B knockdown triggered a significant enrichment in the expression of MAFB-dependent genes.
source: GSK3A/B knockdown triggered a significant enrichment in the expression of MAFB-dependent genes (Figure 4F), genes acquired along the monocyte-to-M-MØ differentiation (Figure 4G), and genes that mark M-MØ, while reducing the expression of GM-MØ-specific genes (Figure 4G).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of MAFB-dependent genes after knockdown

claim: GSK3A/B knockdown enhanced the expression of genes acquired along the monocyte-to-M-MØ differentiation.
source: GSK3A/B knockdown triggered a significant enrichment in the expression of MAFB-dependent genes (Figure 4F), genes acquired along the monocyte-to-M-MØ differentiation (Figure 4G), and genes that mark M-MØ, while reducing the expression of GM-MØ-specific genes (Figure 4G).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of monocyte-to-M-MØ differentiation genes

claim: GSK3A/B knockdown reduced the expression of GM-MØ-specific genes.
source: GSK3A/B knockdown triggered a significant enrichment in the expression of MAFB-dependent genes (Figure 4F), genes acquired along the monocyte-to-M-MØ differentiation (Figure 4G), and genes that mark M-MØ, while reducing the expression of GM-MØ-specific genes (Figure 4G).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing downregulation of GM-MØ-specific genes

claim: GSK3A/B knockdown enhanced the expression of gene sets that define pathogenic pro-fibrotic macrophage subsets in severe COVID-19.
source: Furthermore, in agreement with the effect of CHIR-99021, GSK3A/B knockdown enhanced the expression of the MoMac-VERSE macrophage clusters HES1_Mac (#2) and TREM2_Mac (#3) 2 (Figure 4H) as well as the gene sets that define pathogenic pro-fibrotic macrophage subsets in severe COVID-19 ([SPP1+, GSE145926] [Liao et al., 2020], MoAM3 [GSE155249] [Grant et al., 2021] or CD163+/LGMN+ MØ [EGAS00001005634] [Wendisch et al., 2021]) (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of COVID-19 pathogenic macrophage gene sets after knockdown

claim: Silencing of GSK3A and GSK3B drastically reduced the expression of gene sets that characterize tissue-resident lung alveolar macrophages in COVID-19.
source: Conversely, silencing of GSK3A and GSK3B drastically reduced the expression of the gene sets that characterize tissue-resident lung alveolar macrophages in COVID-19, with the concomitant silencing of GSK3A and GSK3B again showing a stronger effect (Figure 4I).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing downregulation of alveolar macrophage gene sets

claim: Monocytes exposed to CHIR-99021 for 16 hr exhibited increased MAFB levels.
source: To that end, monocytes were exposed to CHIR-99021, and the resulting cells (CHIR-Mon, Figure 5A) exhibited increased MAFB levels as early as 16 hr post-treatment (Figure 5B).
evidence: Western blot data showing increased MAFB in monocytes after 16 hr CHIR-99021 treatment

claim: 16 hr exposure of monocytes to GSK3 inhibitor induced significant alterations in the expression of over 2000 genes.
source: Remarkably, the 16 hr exposure to the GSK3 inhibitor induced significant alterations in the expression of over 2000 genes ([log2FC]>1; adjp<0.05) (Figure 5C) and sufficed to augment the expression of M-MØ-specific genes and genes upregulated during M-CSF-dependent monocyte-to-M-MØ differentiation (Figure 5D), including CCL2, CD163, and IL10 (Figure 5E).
evidence: RNA-Seq data showing differential gene expression in monocytes after CHIR-99021 treatment

claim: The transcriptome of CHIR-Mon exhibited a significant enrichment in MAFB-dependent genes.
source: Notably, the transcriptome of CHIR-Mon exhibited a significant enrichment in MAFB-dependent genes (Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and genes characterizing the MAFB+ pathogenic macrophages in severe COVID-19 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), whereas it showed an under-representation of genes inhibited by MAFB (Simón-Fuentes et al., 2023; Figure 5F).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of MAFB-dependent genes in CHIR-treated monocytes

claim: CHIR-99021 treatment upregulated the expression of 25% of M-MØ-specific genes in monocytes.
source: Compared to DMSO, CHIR-99021 treatment upregulated the expression of 25% of M-MØ-specific genes, including MAFB-dependent genes like CCL2, IL10, and CD163, while downregulating 30% of GM-MØ-specific genes (Figure 5G), and this transcriptional effect was also evident in comparison with M-CSF-treated monocytes (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: RNA-Seq data analysis showing overlap between upregulated genes and M-MØ markers

claim: CHIR-99021 treatment downregulated 30% of GM-MØ-specific genes in monocytes.
source: Compared to DMSO, CHIR-99021 treatment upregulated the expression of 25% of M-MØ-specific genes, including MAFB-dependent genes like CCL2, IL10, and CD163, while downregulating 30% of GM-MØ-specific genes (Figure 5G), and this transcriptional effect was also evident in comparison with M-CSF-treated monocytes (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: RNA-Seq data analysis showing overlap between downregulated genes and GM-MØ markers

claim: CHIR-99021-treated monocytes in the presence of rheumatoid arthritis synovial fluid exhibited enhanced expression of MAFB.
source: Evaluation of CHIR-99021-treated monocytes in the presence of RASF revealed an enhanced expression of MAFB (Figure 5I) and MAFB-dependent genes such as IL10 and LGMN (Figure 5J).
evidence: Western blot data showing increased MAFB in monocytes treated with CHIR-99021 in RASF

claim: CHIR-99021-treated monocytes in the presence of rheumatoid arthritis synovial fluid exhibited enhanced expression of IL10 and LGMN.
source: Evaluation of CHIR-99021-treated monocytes in the presence of RASF revealed an enhanced expression of MAFB (Figure 5I) and MAFB-dependent genes such as IL10 and LGMN (Figure 5J).
evidence: RT-PCR data showing increased IL10 and LGMN expression with statistical significance

claim: GSK3 inhibition in ex vivo isolated human alveolar macrophages results in 865 differentially expressed genes.
source: A total of 865 differentially expressed genes ([log2FC]>1; adjp<0.05) were identified, with 316 genes upregulated in CHIR-AMØ (Figure 6B).
evidence: RNA-Seq data analysis of ex vivo alveolar macrophages after CHIR-99021 treatment

claim: GSK3 inhibition in alveolar macrophages upregulated gene sets that define pathogenic pro-fibrotic macrophage subsets in severe COVID-19.
source: Further comparisons and gene ontology analysis revealed that GSK3 inhibition by CHIR-99021 (CHIR-AMØ) upregulated the gene sets that define pathogenic pro-fibrotic macrophage subsets in severe COVID-19 ([SPP1+, GSE145926] [Liao et al., 2020], MoAM3 [GSE155249] [Grant et al., 2021], or CD163+/LGMN+ MØ [EGAS00001005634] [Wendisch et al., 2021]) (Figure 6C and D; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of COVID-19 pathogenic macrophage gene sets in CHIR-treated alveolar macrophages

claim: CHIR-AMØ exhibited a reduced expression of gene sets that characterize lung-resident alveolar macrophages in severe COVID-19.
source: Conversely, CHIR-AMØ exhibited a reduced expression of the gene sets that characterize lung-resident AMØ in severe COVID-19 ([AMØ1+AMØ2 clusters from EGAS00001005634] [Wendisch et al., 2021], FABP4+ from GSE145926 [Liao et al., 2020], TRAM1 from GSE155249 [Grant et al., 2021]) (Figure 6D and E; Figure 6—figure supplement 2), including key AMØ-specific genes like FABP4 and MARCO (Figure 6E), and similar results were seen upon analysis of AMØ-specific gene sets from other studies (Grant et al., 2021; Melms et al., 2021).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing downregulation of alveolar macrophage gene sets

claim: CHIR-AMØ exhibited higher expression of MAFB.
source: Consistent with these findings, CHIR-AMØ exhibited higher expression of MAFB (Figure 6F), whose increase correlated with an augmented secretion of Legumain, CCL2, and IL-10 (Figure 6G), although the latter was only seen in two samples, probably reflecting heterogeneity in primary cell responses.
evidence: Western blot data showing increased MAFB in CHIR-treated alveolar macrophages

claim: CHIR-AMØ showed augmented secretion of Legumain and CCL2.
source: Consistent with these findings, CHIR-AMØ exhibited higher expression of MAFB (Figure 6F), whose increase correlated with an augmented secretion of Legumain, CCL2, and IL-10 (Figure 6G), although the latter was only seen in two samples, probably reflecting heterogeneity in primary cell responses.
evidence: ELISA data showing increased Legumain and CCL2 secretion

claim: CHIR-AMØ showed lower levels of Activin A in conditioned medium.
source: In contrast, lower levels of Activin A were detected in CHIR-AMØ-conditioned medium (Figure 6G).
evidence: ELISA data showing decreased Activin A levels

claim: The level of phosphorylated Ser21-GSK3α is significantly augmented in lung macrophages from severe COVID-19 patients.
source: Remarkably, and in agreement with the shift in macrophage subsets that takes place in severe COVID-19 lungs (loss of AMØ, appearance of monocyte-derived pro-fibrotic macrophages) (Vega et al., 2020; Wendisch et al., 2021; Liao et al., 2020; Grant et al., 2021), the level of phosphorylated Ser21-GSK3α and Ser9-GSK3β was very significantly augmented in lung macrophages (CD68+) from severe COVID-19 patients, an increase that correlated with a robust enhancement of the macrophage expression of both MAFB and the MAFB-dependent protein CD163 (Figure 6H).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy data showing increased phosphorylated GSK3 in COVID-19 lung macrophages with statistical significance (p<0.001)

claim: The level of phosphorylated Ser9-GSK3β is significantly augmented in lung macrophages from severe COVID-19 patients.
source: Remarkably, and in agreement with the shift in macrophage subsets that takes place in severe COVID-19 lungs (loss of AMØ, appearance of monocyte-derived pro-fibrotic macrophages) (Vega et al., 2020; Wendisch et al., 2021; Liao et al., 2020; Grant et al., 2021), the level of phosphorylated Ser21-GSK3α and Ser9-GSK3β was very significantly augmented in lung macrophages (CD68+) from severe COVID-19 patients, an increase that correlated with a robust enhancement of the macrophage expression of both MAFB and the MAFB-dependent protein CD163 (Figure 6H).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy data showing increased phosphorylated GSK3 in COVID-19 lung macrophages with statistical significance (p<0.001)

claim: Lung macrophages from severe COVID-19 patients show robust enhancement of MAFB expression.
source: Remarkably, and in agreement with the shift in macrophage subsets that takes place in severe COVID-19 lungs (loss of AMØ, appearance of monocyte-derived pro-fibrotic macrophages) (Vega et al., 2020; Wendisch et al., 2021; Liao et al., 2020; Grant et al., 2021), the level of phosphorylated Ser21-GSK3α and Ser9-GSK3β was very significantly augmented in lung macrophages (CD68+) from severe COVID-19 patients, an increase that correlated with a robust enhancement of the macrophage expression of both MAFB and the MAFB-dependent protein CD163 (Figure 6H).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy data showing increased MAFB in COVID-19 lung macrophages with statistical significance (p<0.001)

claim: Lung macrophages from severe COVID-19 patients show robust enhancement of CD163 expression.
source: Remarkably, and in agreement with the shift in macrophage subsets that takes place in severe COVID-19 lungs (loss of AMØ, appearance of monocyte-derived pro-fibrotic macrophages) (Vega et al., 2020; Wendisch et al., 2021; Liao et al., 2020; Grant et al., 2021), the level of phosphorylated Ser21-GSK3α and Ser9-GSK3β was very significantly augmented in lung macrophages (CD68+) from severe COVID-19 patients, an increase that correlated with a robust enhancement of the macrophage expression of both MAFB and the MAFB-dependent protein CD163 (Figure 6H).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy data showing increased CD163 in COVID-19 lung macrophages with statistical significance (p<0.001)

claim: Genes upregulated upon inhibition of GSK3 show higher expression in interstitial macrophages compared to alveolar macrophages.
source: The comparison of IMØ and AMØ subsets revealed that the genes upregulated upon inhibition of GSK3 include numerous MAFB-dependent genes (e.g. MAFB, IL10, LGMN, SPP1, CCL2) and showed a higher expression in IMØ (Figure 7C).
evidence: Single-cell RNA-Seq data analysis comparing gene expression between IMØ and AMØ

claim: Genes downregulated by CHIR-99021 are preferentially or exclusively expressed in alveolar macrophages.
source: On the other hand, the genes downregulated by CHIR-99021 were preferentially or exclusively expressed in AMØ, including INHBA, GSN, FBP1, PPARG, AXL, and AQP3 (Figure 7C).
evidence: Single-cell RNA-Seq data analysis showing AMØ-specific expression of downregulated genes

claim: GSK3 inhibition in GM-MØ significantly enhanced the expression of MAFB-dependent IMØ-specific genes.
source: Further GSEA evidenced that GSK3 inhibition in either GM-MØ (CHIR-GM-MØ) (Figure 7E) or AMØ (CHIR-AMØ) (Figure 7F) very significantly enhanced the expression of MAFB-dependent IMØ-specific genes (as defined by Morse et al., 2019, or by Li, 2022), while simultaneously impairing the expression of genes characterizing human AMØ (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of IMØ-specific genes in CHIR-GM-MØ

claim: GSK3 inhibition in GM-MØ impaired the expression of genes characterizing human alveolar macrophages.
source: Further GSEA evidenced that GSK3 inhibition in either GM-MØ (CHIR-GM-MØ) (Figure 7E) or AMØ (CHIR-AMØ) (Figure 7F) very significantly enhanced the expression of MAFB-dependent IMØ-specific genes (as defined by Morse et al., 2019, or by Li, 2022), while simultaneously impairing the expression of genes characterizing human AMØ (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing downregulation of AMØ-specific genes in CHIR-GM-MØ

claim: GSK3 inhibition in alveolar macrophages significantly enhanced the expression of MAFB-dependent IMØ-specific genes.
source: Further GSEA evidenced that GSK3 inhibition in either GM-MØ (CHIR-GM-MØ) (Figure 7E) or AMØ (CHIR-AMØ) (Figure 7F) very significantly enhanced the expression of MAFB-dependent IMØ-specific genes (as defined by Morse et al., 2019, or by Li, 2022), while simultaneously impairing the expression of genes characterizing human AMØ (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of IMØ-specific genes in CHIR-AMØ

claim: GSK3 inhibition in alveolar macrophages impaired the expression of genes characterizing human alveolar macrophages.
source: Further GSEA evidenced that GSK3 inhibition in either GM-MØ (CHIR-GM-MØ) (Figure 7E) or AMØ (CHIR-AMØ) (Figure 7F) very significantly enhanced the expression of MAFB-dependent IMØ-specific genes (as defined by Morse et al., 2019, or by Li, 2022), while simultaneously impairing the expression of genes characterizing human AMØ (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing downregulation of AMØ-specific genes in CHIR-AMØ

claim: GSK3A/B silencing in GM-MØ yielded an enhanced expression of IMØ-specific genes.
source: More importantly, a similar effect was observed after GSK3A/B silencing in GM-MØ, which yielded an enhanced expression of IMØ-specific genes and a downregulation of the gene set that defines AMØ (Figure 7G).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing enrichment of IMØ-specific genes after GSK3A/B knockdown

claim: GSK3A/B silencing in GM-MØ yielded a downregulation of the gene set that defines alveolar macrophages.
source: More importantly, a similar effect was observed after GSK3A/B silencing in GM-MØ, which yielded an enhanced expression of IMØ-specific genes and a downregulation of the gene set that defines AMØ (Figure 7G).
evidence: GSEA analysis showing downregulation of AMØ-specific genes after GSK3A/B knockdown

claim: GM-CSF is essential for generating lung alveolar macrophages.
source: In fact, GM-CSF is essential for generating lung alveolar macrophages (Guilliams et al., 2013), crucial for surfactant homeostasis, whereas deficient GM-CSF signaling leads to pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (Trapnell et al., 2009), a condition marked by defective surfactant clearance and disruption of pulmonary homeostasis due to alveolar macrophage dysfunction (Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: Deficient GM-CSF signaling leads to pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.
source: In fact, GM-CSF is essential for generating lung alveolar macrophages (Guilliams et al., 2013), crucial for surfactant homeostasis, whereas deficient GM-CSF signaling leads to pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (Trapnell et al., 2009), a condition marked by defective surfactant clearance and disruption of pulmonary homeostasis due to alveolar macrophage dysfunction (Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: M-CSF promotes the development of pro-fibrotic pathogenic monocyte-derived macrophages in lung pathologies like idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
source: Conversely, M-CSF gives rise to anti-inflammatory, pro-resolving, and immunosuppressive monocyte-derived macrophages (M-MØ) (Mulder et al., 2021; Donadon et al., 2020) but promotes the development of pro-fibrotic pathogenic monocyte-derived macrophages in lung pathologies like idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Joshi et al., 2020) and severe COVID-19 (Vega et al., 2020).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: M-CSF promotes the development of pro-fibrotic pathogenic monocyte-derived macrophages in severe COVID-19.
source: Conversely, M-CSF gives rise to anti-inflammatory, pro-resolving, and immunosuppressive monocyte-derived macrophages (M-MØ) (Mulder et al., 2021; Donadon et al., 2020) but promotes the development of pro-fibrotic pathogenic monocyte-derived macrophages in lung pathologies like idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Joshi et al., 2020) and severe COVID-19 (Vega et al., 2020).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: Severe COVID-19 is characterized by a huge increase in monocyte-derived M-MØ and a reduction of tissue-resident GM-MØ-like lung macrophages.
source: The pathological relevance of GM-MØ and M-MØ subsets is evident in severe COVID-19, with a huge increase in monocyte-derived M-MØ and a reduction of tissue-resident GM-MØ-like lung macrophages (Wendisch et al., 2021; Liao et al., 2020; Grant et al., 2021).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: MAFB determines the transcriptional and functional specification of monocyte-derived M-MØ.
source: Our prior research has established that MAFB determines the transcriptional and functional specification of monocyte-derived M-MØ, characterized by significantly higher MAFB levels compared to GM-MØ (Cuevas et al., 2017).
evidence: Prior research by the authors as cited

claim: The protein levels of large MAF family members are controlled through GSK3 phosphorylation-dependent proteasome degradation.
source: Since the protein levels of large MAF family members (MAF, MAFA, MAFB, NRL) are controlled through GSK3 phosphorylation-dependent proteasome degradation (Eychène et al., 2008), we initially assessed the relative levels of the inhibitory (Ser21 for GSK3α and Ser9 for GSK3β) and activation-associated (Tyr279 for GSK3α and Tyr216 for GSK3β) phosphorylation of GSK3 in M-MØ and GM-MØ.
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: The homeostatic and reparative transcriptional profile of human M-MØ is orchestrated by MAF and MAFB.
source: In this regard, recent findings indicate that the homeostatic and reparative transcriptional profile of human M-MØ is orchestrated by MAF and MAFB (Cuevas et al., 2017; Kim, 2017; Kang et al., 2017), closely related transcription factors that regulate stemness and self-renewal in the mouse hematopoietic lineage (Eychène et al., 2008; Lavin et al., 2014; Kelly et al., 2000; Aziz et al., 2009; Soucie et al., 2016; Sarrazin et al., 2009).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: MAFB influences IL-10 production in M-MØ.
source: In fact, the distinctive expression of MAFB in M-MØ, influencing IL-10 production (Cuevas et al., 2017; Cuevas et al., 2022), also mediates macrophage reprogramming induced by methotrexate (Ríos et al., 2023) and LXR ligands (de la Aleja et al., 2023).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: MAFB mediates macrophage reprogramming induced by methotrexate.

claim: Modulating GSK3 activity could offer a viable avenue for reprogramming monocyte-derived macrophages.
source: Given the pivotal role of MAFB/MAF in human macrophage functional specification, and considering the regulation of large MAF factors through GSK3-mediated phosphorylation-induced proteasomal degradation (Eychène et al., 2008), we hypothesized that modulating GSK3 activity could offer a viable avenue for reprogramming monocyte-derived macrophages.
evidence: Hypothesis based on established knowledge and reasoning

claim: Inhibiting GSK3 shifts the gene profile of alveolar macrophages toward that of interstitial macrophages.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that inhibiting GSK3 shifts the gene profile of alveolar macrophages toward that of interstitial macrophages (or monocyte-derived macrophages), and imply that the activation status of GSK3 significantly influences the specification of lung-resident macrophages (AMØ vs. IMØ).
evidence: Summary conclusion from multiple experimental findings

claim: The activation status of GSK3 significantly influences the specification of lung-resident macrophages (AMØ vs. IMØ).
source: Altogether, these results indicate that inhibiting GSK3 shifts the gene profile of alveolar macrophages toward that of interstitial macrophages (or monocyte-derived macrophages), and imply that the activation status of GSK3 significantly influences the specification of lung-resident macrophages (AMØ vs. IMØ).

claim: The GSK3-MAFB axis is a therapeutic target for macrophage reprogramming.
source: Since pathogenic lung macrophages in severe COVID-19 exhibit high levels of inactive GSK3 and heightened levels of MAFB and MAFB-dependent proteins, our results underscore the potent macrophage reprogramming impact of GSK3 inhibition and highlight the GSK3-MAFB axis as a promising therapeutic target for macrophage reprogramming.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental findings and clinical observations

claim: Macrophage PI3Kγ inactivates GSK3 via phosphorylation of Ser9 (GSK3β) and Ser21 (GSK3α).
source: The ability of PI3Kγ to toggle between immune stimulation and suppression aligns with our findings on GSK3 inhibition, as PI3Kγ inactivates GSK3 via phosphorylation of Ser9 (GSK3β) and Ser21 (GSK3α) (Eychène et al., 2008).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: GSK3 inhibition may contribute to the anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects of PI3Kγ inactivation by enhancing MAFB expression.

claim: MAFB might participate in the macrophage reprogramming consequences of mTOR modulation.
source: Moreover, MAFB might even participate in the macrophage reprogramming consequences of mTOR modulation (Byles et al., 2013; Do et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023) due to the known reciprocal interactions between GSK3 and mTOR (Evangelisti et al., 2020).

claim: GSK3 inhibitors redirect the GM-CSF+IL-4-dependent development of monocyte-derived dendritic cells toward the generation of macrophage-like cells.
source: The significant impact of GSK3 inhibition by CHIR-99021 on the macrophage transcriptional profile mirrors the effects observed with other GSK3 inhibitors on the differentiation of monocyte-derived dendritic cells (MDDCs) (Rodionova et al., 2007). Specifically, GSK3 inhibitors like LiCl, SB415286, or SB216763 redirect the GM-CSF+IL-4-dependent development of MDDC toward the generation of macrophage-like cells (Rodionova et al., 2007).
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: MAFB expression is higher in monocyte-derived macrophages than in dendritic cells.
source: Considering that MAFB expression is higher in monocyte-derived macrophages than in dendritic cells (Bakri et al., 2005), it is reasonable to infer that GSK3 inhibitors also boost MAFB expression in cells differentiated in the presence of GM-CSF+IL-4, thereby supporting the modulation of GSK3 activity as a tool to alter lineage determination in myeloid cells.
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature

claim: MAFB serves as a negative regulator of GM-CSF signaling.
source: Given that MAFB serves as a negative regulator of GM-CSF signaling (Koshida et al., 2015), downregulation of MAFB expression through modulation of GSK3 activity emerges as a rationale strategy to re-direct pathogenic monocyte-derived macrophages toward the acquisition of a lung-resident alveolar macrophage-like profile during severe COVID-19.
evidence: Established knowledge from cited literature
